expectations.evidence: In §6's draft, nearly every entry carries a colon-suffixed note that names concrete contents rather than selling: "Install the Web SDK ... package name, init snippet, first pageview event"; "Identify users ... linking anonymous and identified traffic without double-counting"; "Track events ... event schema, required fields, idempotency keys"; "Consent and privacy ... GDPR/CCPA gating before first track call"; "Error codes ... every error string, its cause, its fix"; "Rate limits ... thresholds, backoff, retry-after header"; "Webhooks ... inbound destination signature verification". expectations.text: Writes each entry note as a routing signal describing what the reader will find, not as marketing copy
expectations.evidence: Every entry note is a functional descriptor of page contents, not promotional language. Examples: 'Install an SDK and send your first event in under 10 minutes'; 'Events, properties, users, and the data pipeline, in one page'; '`identify`, anonymous-to-known merge, and alias resolution'; 'Auth, rate limits, and base URLs'; 'What not to send, redaction, and retention controls'; 'Mapping Segment's spec to Brightloom's event model'. Notes disambiguate between similar entries (Node.js vs Python SDK both 'Server-side tracking and batching'; JS/iOS/Android differentiated by language and capture mode
